gaps.explanation: The revenue detail lines come from the p8 'Supplementary Budgetary Comparison Schedule for All Funds Combined - Modified Cash Basis'. It is an all-funds (governmental + utility) cash-receipts schedule, Total Revenues and Transfers 197,207. Its 'Claims, Refunds, Reimbursements, and Other Local Receipts' 100,403 holds the utility fund's cash receipts as well as the governmental other receipts. The governmental funds statement p4 prints Total Revenues 141,433. Arithmetic: p4 governmental other receipts (Interest 5,479 + Dividend 1,766 + Electrical Distribution System Lease 33,975 + Charges For Services 2,365 + Claims, Reimbursements, and Refunds 165 + Licenses and Permits 956) = 44,706. 100,403 - 44,706 = 55,697 = utility cash receipts (p7: Receipts from Customers 51,178 + Customer Utility Deposits 150 + Interest 4,369). p8 Sales Tax 23,938 vs p4 23,861 = +77. 55,697 + 77 = 55,774 = gap. The schedule prints no split by fund, so no exact detail fix is possible.

The utility fund prints Total Revenues 51,140 + Net Nonoperating Revenues 4,369 = 55,509 on p6. It has no separate schedule. Its receipts are inside the p8 all-funds combined budget schedule line 'Claims, Refunds, Reimbursements, and Other Local Receipts' 100,403 (tagged governmental), on a cash basis: 55,697 (p7: 51,178 + 150 + 4,369). The difference from p6 is the accrual/cash difference (p5 Sales Tax Payable 188). Adding p6 lines would count the same money twice. No fix.

The p8 all-funds budget schedule line 'Utility' 61,023 is cash paid: p7 Payments to Suppliers 52,215 + Payments to Employees 8,808 = 61,023. The p6 proprietary statement prints Total Expenses 61,828, which includes Depreciation 774 and accruals of 31 (Salaries 8,839 vs cash 8,808). 61,023 + 774 + 31 = 61,828; gap 805. Both printed totals are correct on their own basis.
